steps.content: WhiteSands stretches endlessly to the horizon. The blazing sun pours shimmering heat waves above the scorching sands. No living creature would dare traverse these dunes at this high noon.
Except this man. He's clad in desert gear stolen from the merchant caravan, its thick insulation layer and cooling circulation system allowing him to survive the lonely trek across WhiteSands.
His pack, once bulging with supplies, now hangs nearly empty. Only one last bottle of water and a few hardtacks remain.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Hah... hah... How many days so far? Guess... 19?

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: That truck we stole wasn't half bad. Beat up here and there though, still ran fine. Wouldn't have abandoned it if it hadn't run out of fuel.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Been walking for ages, are we? Lost track of time. Going on foot is slow, but we're used to it, aren't we, Evelo? Just like when we marched against desert bandits and disasters back then.
The man stops to adjust his pack as if still carrying some heavy burden, tightening the straps across his shoulders. The grotesque scar on the back of his hand is clearly visible.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: No weapons, no commanders with a functioning brain... and of course, no Hypercubes. We used to envy DisCity's FAC so much. Heard each of their soldiers got plenty.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: But what could we do? Our poor little town kept gambling on our lives, one after another. After you all died, it didn't take long for the whole party to fall apart... Hah, that's when I finally saw my chance to escape.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: I ran into that woman called Vautour Bleu and her caravan. Said she could take me to DisCity to live that "good life," but only if we make a deal first.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: To hell with her deal, f*** liar. That woman never planned to go to DisCity. She thinks I'm easy to fool around, huh? Ain't she the most useless one in the caravan?
His body and mind teeter on the edge of collapse, his legs driven forward by nothing but hollow hope and burning hatred.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: I stole their car, got us water and food, even their cargo. Took that navigation device off the car too.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Once I reach DisCity, I'm gonna sell this gear. That should give us enough money to settle down there.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: If only we'd had gear like this back then... It'd probably have cost an arm and a leg, but at least Belmar would survive.

steps.speaker: Evelo
steps.content: That's right. Keep moving, Lyman. You must make it to DisCity. Do it for us.
He rubs his eyes, and through the writhing heat wave, he sees a few swaying familiar silhouettes. They wave to him, and one approaches, reaching out as if to help him up.

steps.speaker: Belmar
steps.content: Go, Lyman. We can't make it to DisCity, but you will. See that promised land for all of us.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: ...You bastards.
Lady Hypatia.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Just don't go yet... Stay with me, a little longer...

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Sir, we've got someone at the checkpoint. He's from WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Just one person? Not with a caravan? That's a restricted zone. How could he make it through?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Confirmed, it's just him. No anomalies detected in the surrounding area, his M-value within the safe range. Might be a refugee who got separated from the group.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: It could also be a disguised Corruptor, or a spy from Outlands... Stay alert. Let's go and have a look.
At the foot of the border wall, Lyman lifts his head in a daze, confronted by the towering barrier that cuts off everything beyond.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: So this is... DisCity...

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Here, our dreams... we're finally here...
Before he becomes aware of the situation, several heavily armed soldiers appear and surround him.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Name? Age? Where are you from?

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: ...Ly... Leonard. 30 years. I'm an... engineer. I'm from DisCity... was sent to Désir for a commission... I was heading home to visit my family when the desert bandits attacked.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: No matter what happens, time always takes on the same appearance in my hands. Yesterday, today, tomorrow, every day... nothing ever changes.
He recites the details of the fake identity Vautour Bleu forged for him two weeks ago.
Having no idea what kind of place Désir is, he can only dodge the guard's questions about its details by playing up his exhaustion and mental confusion.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: I'm an engineer from DisCity! My family's waiting for me!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: We'll let you through once we verify your identity. Hold out your hand.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: What...
He watches stupidly as the guard takes his hand, collecting fingerprints and a blood sample to match with the database. An ominous chill crawls up his spine.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Sir, your DNA profile says your name's Lyman. You're no engineer. You're an active Outland soldier.
Clack. The familiar sound of guns being loaded pierces the air as multiple black barrels point simultaneously at Lyman.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Hands up! You are under suspicion of espionage and illegal entry. You are under arrest by the DisCity Border Guard!

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: That's impossible! She promised me, she said she'd set it up for me... No, I-I'm not Lyman. My name is Leonard! I'm an engineer from DisCity!

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Look, this is our company uniform. This proves for me!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Who do you mean by she?

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: She... Sh-she's...
Lyman still hasn't gotten over his grueling journey. He stares around in confusion, his muscles still twitching from the memory of constant exertion, eventually going into spasm.
Lyman collapses to his knees. When he raises his head, all he can see are the cold gun barrels pointed at him from every corner of the area.
That's when his dignity crumbles.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Please, please... Mercy please! Just let me in! I'm not a spy. I spent a whole month crawling through WhiteSands to get here!

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: I swear I mean no harm to DisCity! I just want a life. A life with no Mania and disasters!

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Y...you can lock me up, Sir. Do me investigation, as long as you want! Just please don't send me back. I can't go back to that hell!
Lyman gazes hopefully at the commissioner's pampered face, so different from the weathered, battle-worn features of even the highest-ranking officer he's ever seen.

DisCity's prosperity and peace are laid bare before him in the most visceral way. He's willing to cast aside every shred of his ego, begging this official for just a touch of the magnanimity befitting such a great city.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: I regret to inform you, Mr. Lyman, that your actions constitute illegal entry. Moreover, your military status complicates matters as it interferes with Outland political protocols.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Therefore, we will deport you after notifying your home city. Until we're ready for that, you shall remain here.
The commissioner's hollow, bureaucratic sympathy crushes Lyman's last bit of hope, his features contorting with horror and despair.

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: Deport me? No, I'm not going back. I'll die there! There's nothing there but suffering!
If I'm going to die... If I'm going to die anyway...!
He leaps up in a frenzy, breaking free of his restraints and charging toward the checkpoint.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: Watch out! He's forcing through!

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Stop him! Snipers, get ready.
Deaf to all warnings, Lyman fixes his eyes only on the barrier ahead, a fragile obstacle that seems so easy to break through.
It's there. Right there.
Everyone's dreams and hopes. The oases and springs that carried him through WhiteSands. Lying right there.
Let me through. Just let me through...!
Stop!! Stop there!! Don't...
BANG—!
Vautour Bleu's pen slips, slicing through the letter paper with a sharp, piercing scratch.
Both pen and paper, her loyal companions in the past two weeks, are now ruined, like a sign of something imminent.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: ...Ruined, after all.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Looks like the ending won't change no matter who's holding the pen.
With a soft sigh, she discards the spoiled paper and pen, deciding to abandon the letter altogether.
As the haze dances and fades before her eyes, she thinks she sees those long-lost young faces from her memories.
Those hopeful souls who once journeyed with her to DisCity, they too perished along the way.
There will always be gamblers willing to bet their lives on hollow dreams.
And yet...
And yet.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Boss, is everything alright? You don't look well.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Nothing. Just reminiscing about the past. Anything new?

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Yes. In fact, we... we've been surrounded!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Look at you, boy, you're practically shaking. It's not the first time we get a run-in with desert bandits.
Catching Vautour Bleu's indifference, the assistant lowers his voice anxiously.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: No, this time it's not just some petty bandits. It's the FAC from DisCity! They're saying... you're involved in sneaking some Outland deserter into DisCity!

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: They've hit you with some serious charges, like um... motivating illegals and disrupting Outland relations? They want to take you in for questioning!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Oh? The FAC from DisCity?
A flicker of surprise crosses Vautour Bleu's face, but it quickly gives way to bitter realization.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: For them to come now, it must be about that incident. I was even counting on that kid. To change the ending of the story...? Just being naive I am, heh.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Well then, a deal is a deal. It's time for me to hold up my end of the bargain.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Boss! Are you really going? But if you leave now, the caravan...
The split second of bitter realization vanishes, and right in the next moment, her characteristic self-assured smile returns to her face.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: No need to worry, boy. They just want me to assist with their investigation. I'll be back once it's done. While I'm away, continue along the route as planned.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: You might not get the best deals without me doing the talking... But think of it as a chance to practice. I don't expect you to make a fortune anyway. Just try not to lose money while I'm away.

Night has fallen. In the dim light, the caravan crew sit around their campfires, some clutching ladles and spatulas, others holding bowls and spoons, all glaring viciously at the FAC operatives standing in their midst.

It almost seems one word from Vautour Bleu would send her people charging in with their makeshift weapons. And it is in this tense atmosphere that the caravan's owner approaches the FAC operatives with graceful tardiness.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Vautour Bleu, correct? We might need you to go with us to DisCity, and assist with our investigation.
In the flickering firelight, the FAC soldier's face is expressionless like a machine and the voice that comes out is also utterly flat.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Sure thing. Cooperating with the authorities is the sacred duty of a humble merchant like myself. Though I must admit that I'm quite curious, how did you manage to find me?

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: That's not a question we can answer. But you have the right to ask the person in charge once we arrive in DisCity.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Sometimes being flexible might serve you better, sir. That Chief of yours at the MBCC knows how to play the game.
She raises a hand to quiet her restless crew, her smile remaining as gentle as ever.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Well then, shall we go, little bloodhounds?
